proposals.before: His birth name was Dao Yuan; he changed it to avoid the Founder's taboo on the character yuan.
proposals.after: His birth name was Dao Yuan; he changed it to avoid the Founder's partial taboo on the character dao.
proposals.reason: The original name 道淵 was changed because of 太祖偏諱; Xiao Daocheng's given name is 道成, so the avoided graph is 道, and the surviving name 淵 shows that yuan was not the taboo.

proposals.before: When Shen Youzhi rose, the Founder went into the hall of court; Prince of Yuzhang Liao held the eastern headquarters in his place and set Yuan at the head of troops encamped at the minister of public works' left quarters, dividing the capital for defense.
proposals.after: When Shen Youzhi rose, the Founder went into the hall of court; Prince of Yuzhang Yi held the eastern headquarters in his place and set Yuan at the head of troops encamped at the minister of public works' left quarters, dividing the capital for defense.
proposals.reason: The personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Liao; Liao is a phonetic error in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the Founder entered the hall of court; the Prince of Yuzhang, Liao, held the Eastern headquarters in his stead and had Yuan lead troops to encamp at the Minister of Public Works' left quarters, dividing forces to guard the capital.
proposals.after: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the Founder entered the hall of court; the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, held the Eastern headquarters in his stead and had Yuan lead troops to encamp at the Minister of Public Works' left quarters, dividing forces to guard the capital.
proposals.reason: The personal name 嶷 is Yi; the literal English wrongly gives Liao.

proposals.before: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; Prince of Yuzhang Liao climbed the western gate at night and hailed Yuan from afar; Yuan started up in alarm, led his host to the crisis, and was first at Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
proposals.after: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; Prince of Yuzhang Yi climbed the western gate at night and hailed Yuan from afar; Yuan started up in alarm, led his host to the crisis, and was first at Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
proposals.reason: The personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Liao.

proposals.before: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; the Prince of Yuzhang, Liao, climbed the western gate at night and called Yuan from afar; Yuan sprang up in alarm, led his army to the crisis, and was first to reach Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
proposals.after: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, climbed the western gate at night and called Yuan from afar; Yuan sprang up in alarm, led his army to the crisis, and was first to reach Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
proposals.reason: The personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Liao.

proposals.before: The northern enemy sent the false general Xue Daobiao against Shouchun; because Daobiao was Yuan's close kin, the Founder instructed Liu Huaishuai, administrator of Qi: "I hear Daobiao is plainly on his way; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one household. For men like this, spare no trick from every side—even if they do not wholly believe you, it is enough to set wolves and jackals doubting one another."
proposals.after: The northern enemy sent the false general Xue Daobiao against Shouchun; because Daobiao was Yuan's close kin, the Founder instructed Liu Huaiwei, administrator of Qi: "I hear Daobiao is plainly on his way; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one household. For men like this, spare no trick from every side—even if they do not wholly believe you, it is enough to set wolves and jackals doubting one another."
proposals.reason: 劉懷慰 is Liu Huaiwei; 慰 is wei, not shuai.

proposals.before: The northerners sent the false general Xue Daobiao to raid Shouchun; because Daobiao was close kin to Yuan, the Founder instructed Liu Huaishuai, administrator of Qi commandery: "I hear Daobiao is plainly coming; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one family. For men of this sort, do not spare many-sided deceptions—even if they do not fully believe them, it is enough to sow doubt among the wolves and jackals."
proposals.after: The northerners sent the false general Xue Daobiao to raid Shouchun; because Daobiao was close kin to Yuan, the Founder instructed Liu Huaiwei, administrator of Qi commandery: "I hear Daobiao is plainly coming; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one family. For men of this sort, do not spare many-sided deceptions—even if they do not fully believe them, it is enough to sow doubt among the wolves and jackals."
proposals.reason: 劉懷慰 is Liu Huaiwei; 慰 is wei, not shuai.

proposals.before: Lang held the mirror a long while and said, "I see death and return home."
proposals.after: Lang held the mirror a long while and said, "To look upon death as going home."
proposals.reason: 視死如歸 is the idiom ‘regard death as returning home,’ not a first-person vision of dying and going home.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as bearer of the staff, overseer of Xu, general who chastises the foe, and governor of northern Xuzhou.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as bearer of the staff, overseer of military affairs in Xu, general who chastises the foe, and governor of northern Xuzhou.
proposals.reason: 督徐州諸軍事 is overseeing Xu military affairs, not a bare ‘overseer of Xu’; the literal line already has the military scope.

proposals.before: A son of heaven who kills a man in a passing fit—what grave crime is that?
proposals.after: A son of the Son of Heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is that?
proposals.reason: 天子兒 is the emperor’s son (the Prince of Badong), not ‘a son of heaven’ as if the killer were the emperor himself.

proposals.before: A son of heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is there?
proposals.after: A son of the Son of Heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is there?
proposals.reason: Same reversal: 天子兒 names the imperial son, matching 巴東王年少 in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: Zhang Houbo of the Eastern Smelting Works tried casting, but with gold barred from the mix the points turned soft and useless, and the plan died.
proposals.after: Zhang Houbo, magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, found the cast metal points blunt and unfit for use, and the plan was not adopted.
proposals.reason: ＜金禁＞ marks the graph 鐖, a metal/arrowhead word, not a ban on gold in the alloy; the English invents a metallurgical prohibition.

proposals.before: The magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, Zhang Houbo, found that casting, under the ban on gold in the alloy, came out dull and unfit for use; the proposal was not adopted,
proposals.after: The magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, Zhang Houbo, found that the cast 鐖-points came out dull and unfit for use; the proposal was not adopted,
proposals.reason: The split graph is 鐖, not ‘ban on gold in the alloy.’

proposals.before: The boy emperor said: "Tonight I want one bed and one woman; come back tomorrow night."
proposals.after: The boy emperor said: "Tonight I mean to take my pleasure in one place; wait until tomorrow night."
proposals.reason: Chinese 欲一處作適 means to take pleasure in one place; the idiomatic English invents a bed and a woman not present in the source.

proposals.before: A saying ran: "Mean to fool Zhang? Ask Huan Kang."
proposals.after: A saying ran: "Want to play the deceiver? Ask Huan Kang."
proposals.reason: 侜張 is a binome meaning to deceive or swagger, not a person named Zhang.

proposals.before: People made a saying of it: "Want to trick Zhang—ask Huan Kang."
proposals.after: People made a saying of it: "Want to deceive—ask Huan Kang."
proposals.reason: 侜張 is an idiom of deception, not the personal name Zhang.

proposals.before: When Jianyuan opened he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggu, with three hundred households.
proposals.after: When Jianyuan opened he was enfeoffed as Nan (viscount) of Pinggu, with three hundred households.
proposals.reason: 平固男 is the nan/male viscount rank, not 伯 (baron); the idiomatic English overstates the title.

proposals.before: At the opening of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggu, with a fief of three hundred households,
proposals.after: At the opening of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Nan of Pinggu county, with a fief of three hundred households,
proposals.reason: 男 is not baron; baron would be 伯 as in 吳平縣伯 in s0134.

proposals.before: For his fighting name he was made Prince Xie of Jinxi's household guard, named acting aide in the campaign-armor bureau, and sent with the Xiakou garrison.
proposals.after: For his fighting name he was made Prince Xie of Jinxi's household guard, named acting aide in the campaign-armor bureau of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and sent with the Xiakou garrison.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 征虜, which names the campaign-armor bureau as belonging to the General Who Punishes the Barbarians; the literal field already keeps that office.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongming, died at sixty-one.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongming, he died at sixty-one.
proposals.reason: The silent Chinese subject 度 is dropped, leaving an ungrammatical English clause without a subject.

proposals.before: Posthumously enfeoffed Supporting-the-State General and Inspector of Liang and Qin.
proposals.after: After death he was granted Supporting-the-State General and inspector of Liang and Qin.
proposals.reason: 贈 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment; the idiomatic field already uses 'honored as'.

proposals.before: Cao Hu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi in Xiapi; in youth he had been called Tiger Head.
proposals.after: Cao Hu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi in Xiapi; his original name was Tiger Head.
proposals.reason: 本名 means original name, not a name used specifically in youth; the idiomatic rendering invents a childhood-stage restriction.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed as Pacifying-the-North General and Administrator of Dongguan.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed Pacifying-the-North General and Administrator of Dongguan.
proposals.reason: 除 in appointment formulae means to confer office, not to remove; the literal reverses the career move.

proposals.before: The emperor told Hu: "Guangling must go to a man at my breast—not to any officer I might name in passing. You cannot keep that post."
proposals.after: The emperor told Hu: "Guangling requires a bosom confidant; anyone I cannot sincerely entrust may not hold this post."
proposals.reason: 非吾意可委者，不可得處此任 states a qualification for the post, not that Hu is being dismissed from Guangling; the idiomatic last sentence reverses the edict.

proposals.before: The emperor issued an edict Hu: "Guangling requires a trusted intimate; not someone I can entrust at will—you cannot hold this post."
proposals.after: The emperor issued an edict to Hu: "Guangling requires a trusted intimate; one I cannot sincerely entrust may not hold this post."
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical (missing to) and, like the idiomatic, turns a trust qualification into a dismissal.

proposals.before: The northern ruler Yuan Hong sent Hu a letter: "The Emperor thanks the false Inspector of Yongzhou: divine fortune shows at the center; the imperial dwelling opens at Luoyang.
proposals.after: The northern ruler Yuan Hong sent Hu a letter: "The Emperor addresses the false Inspector of Yongzhou: divine fortune shows at the center; the imperial dwelling opens at Luoyang.
proposals.reason: 謝 here is the diplomatic formula of notification, not gratitude; literal thanks reverses the verb.

proposals.before: Moreover, north of Han and beside the river, close upon our dry county seat, the phoenix chariot moved first to order our sacred capital.
proposals.after: Moreover, north of Han and beside the river, close upon our imperial county seat, the phoenix chariot moved first to order our sacred capital.
proposals.reason: 乾縣 is the heavenly or imperial seat, not a dry county; 乾 is misread as the weather sense.

proposals.before: If you press on in delusion—advance without knowing when to pull back—bronze gongs will clear the march, cloud-banners will sweep the north, we shall run far through Yan and Dai, leash every crowned name among you, let your young envoy vanish in a breath, and leave Touman without offerings.
proposals.after: If you press on in delusion—advance without knowing when to pull back—bronze gongs will clear the march, cloud-banners will sweep the north, we shall run far through Yan and Dai, leash every crowned name among you, let Shaoqing vanish in a breath, and leave Touman without offerings.
proposals.reason: 少卿 is Li Ling courtesy name Shaoqing, paired with Touman as a classical extinction threat, not a generic young envoy.

proposals.before: If you then persist in error, knowing advance but forgetting retreat, bronze gongs will warn the road, cloud-banners will sweep north, we shall drive far through Yan and Dai, bind together the famed kings, make the young secretary suddenly gone, and Touman receive no sacrifice.
proposals.after: If you then persist in error, knowing advance but forgetting retreat, bronze gongs will warn the road, cloud-banners will sweep north, we shall drive far through Yan and Dai, bind together the famed kings, make Shaoqing suddenly gone, and Touman receive no sacrifice.
proposals.reason: 少卿 is the courtesy name Shaoqing (Li Ling), not an office young secretary.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongtai, he was named supervising censor and Right Guard General, given staff authority, and placed under regional inspector Chen Xianda, who held at Xiangyang to fight the northerners.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongtai, he was named Given-Service Courtier and Right Guard General, given staff authority, and placed under Commander Chen Xianda, who held at Xiangyang to fight the northerners.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is a palace courtier attendant, not a censor; 都督 is commander rather than regional inspector.

decisions.reason: 本名道淵 was changed for 太祖偏諱; Xiao Daocheng's given name is 道成, so the avoided graph is 道, and the surviving name 淵 shows that yuan was not the taboo. The replacement correctly names the partial taboo on dao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 本名道淵，避太祖偏諱改。

The literal repeats Huaishuai for 劉懷慰; Huaiwei is the correct reading of 慰.
視死如歸 is the set phrase ‘regard death as returning home,’ not a first-person report of seeing death and going home. The replacement restores the idiom; the literal field already had it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朗執鏡良久曰：「視死如歸。」

decisions.reason: 督徐州諸軍事 is overseeing military affairs in Xu, not a bare overseer of Xu. Restoring 諸軍事 is a real office correction, not a stylistic tweak.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 出爲持節、督徐州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、北徐州刺史。

decisions.reason: 天子兒 names the emperor’s son (the Prince of Badong in the previous sentence), not the Son of Heaven as killer. 過誤 is a passing error, not a fit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪。

decisions.reason: The literal has the same reversal of 天子兒; the imperial son, matching 巴東王年少, is the agent who killed.

＜金禁＞ is a split graph for 鐖 (arrowhead/metal point), not a ban on gold in the alloy. Wikisource retains the same split; the original English invents a metallurgical prohibition. Adding magistrate restores 東冶令.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 東冶令張候伯以鑄＜金禁＞鈍，不合用，事不行

decisions.reason: The split graph is 鐖, not a gold-alloy ban, but leaving the raw character 鐖 in English is awkward. In context with 鍜箭鏃 / 鑄作, ‘cast arrowheads’ is the complete natural rendering.

decisions.reason: 欲一處作適 means to take pleasure in one place; 待明日夜 is wait until tomorrow night. The original invents a bed and a woman absent from the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝曰：「我今夕欲一處作適，待明日夜。」

decisions.reason: 侜張 is a binome for deception/swagger, not a person named Zhang. The saying pairs that verb with 問桓康.
The literal likewise treats 侜張 as the name Zhang; the replacement restores the idiom of deception.
平固男 is the nan rank (男), not baron (伯, as in 吳平縣伯). The parenthetical viscount correctly identifies the fifth noble rank without changing the place name already used.

decisions.after: At the opening of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Nan of Pinggu, with a fief of three hundred households,
decisions.reason: 男 is not baron, so the rank must change to Nan, but this sentence does not write 縣; adding ‘county’ is unsupported. Keep Pinggu and the original fief phrasing.
征虜鎧曹行參軍 names the campaign-armor bureau of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians. Omitting 征虜 drops a real office element that the literal already keeps.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 除征虜鎧曹行參軍，隨鎮夏口。

decisions.reason: 永明元年，卒，年六十一 has a silent subject (度). Dropping it leaves an ungrammatical English clause; supplying ‘he’ is required and does not add meaning.
贈 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment (封). The idiomatic field already uses ‘honored as’; the literal must not say enfeoffed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贈輔國將軍、梁秦二州刺史。

decisions.reason: 本名虎頭 is an original name, not a name used only in youth. The replacement matches 本名 without inventing a childhood-stage restriction.
尋除寧朔將軍、東莞太守 is an appointment formula: 除 confers office, it does not remove it. The literal had reversed the career move.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尋除寧朔將軍、東莞太守。

decisions.reason: 非吾意可委者，不可得處此任 is a qualification for Guangling (only a trusted intimate may hold it), not a dismissal of Hu. The original last sentence reversed the edict after he had just been made 廣陵太守.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 廣陵須心腹，非吾意可委者，不可得處此任。

decisions.reason: 敕虎曰 needs ‘to Hu’, and the same trust qualification must not be turned into ‘you cannot hold this post’ as a personal dismissal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上敕虎曰：「廣陵須心腹，非吾意可委者，不可得處此任。」

decisions.reason: 皇帝謝偽雍州刺史 is the diplomatic notification formula; 謝 here does not mean thanks. ‘Addresses’ restores the verb; the idiomatic ‘greets’ already avoided gratitude.
乾縣 is the heavenly/imperial seat (乾), not a dry county. The weather reading of 乾 is a factual error.
少卿忽諸 pairs 少卿 (Li Ling’s courtesy name Shaoqing) with 頭曼 as a classical extinction threat, not a generic young envoy.
The literal’s ‘young secretary’ treats 少卿 as an office; it is the courtesy name Shaoqing, parallel to Touman.

decisions.after: In the first year of Yongtai, he was named palace attendant and Right Guard General, given staff authority, and placed under Commander Chen Xianda, who held at Xiangyang to fight the northerners.
decisions.reason: 給事中 is not a censor, and 都督 is not a regional inspector (刺史). The chapter already renders 給事中 as ‘palace attendant’ (s0077). ‘Given-Service Courtier’ is an awkward calque; ‘Commander’ for 都督 is the needed title fix.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷給事中，右衞將軍，持節，隷都督陳顯達停襄陽伐虜。

Accepted r0022 restores 本名 as original/given name. The 虎頭 fact remains; only the childhood-name kind, created by ‘in youth,’ must change.
Revised r0030 shows 給事中 is a palace attendant post, not a supervising censor; the office, date, and evidence are unchanged.
Revised r0030 shows 都督 is commander, not regional inspector (刺史). The Chinese title and person remain.
The office claim’s English label followed the mistranslation of 都督 as regional inspector; commander is the corrected value.
